project.name: libaom / AV1 decoder
project.commit_note: Stage 01 reproduced against the staged checkout at `_work/src/aom` on commit `a92f3c847f445800e631a43bc2ab5894fedbc841`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `493cf67c62441838a56c5ea6f8dfbf6777e3cee7`. Neither metadata commit is an ancestor of the staged tree. The same local repository does contain patch commit `ee9dbcb018f20f16348b22bc413dec1c9d901183` (`Fix issues in row-mt decoding`), and all line anchors below use the staged checkout's still-unfixed row-mt line map.

classification.classification_note: The saved ASan report shows a 4-byte write 44 bytes to the left of the raw malloc chunk backing `cur_sb_col`. Because `dec_row_mt_alloc()` obtains `cur_sb_col` through `aom_malloc()`, which returns an aligned interior pointer from `aom_memalign()`, that runtime fact proves the executed row index was negative and the store landed before the returned `cur_sb_col` array. The exact negative slot is not recovered from the saved artifacts.

staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged checkout, so every source location below is anchored to its exact vulnerable line map.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42508710 (aom): Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 4 found by fuzz target av1_dec_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42508710
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable checkout / local `git show ee9dbcb018f20f16348b22bc413dec1c9d901183`
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced AddressSanitizer's `heap-buffer-overflow` WRITE against the staged checkout `a92f3c847f445800e631a43bc2ab5894fedbc841`, not against the metadata vulnerable commit; all line anchors below use this staged tree, and local git history separately contains patch commit `ee9dbcb018f20f16348b22bc413dec1c9d901183` whose message explains the stale-`xd->mi_row` row-mt bug family. The exact 91-byte witness makes the fuzz harness request 33 decoder threads and pass one truncated 47-byte frame into libaom, so `av1_decode_tg_tiles_and_wrapup()` takes `decode_tiles_row_mt()`. Row-mt parsing materializes a `TileBufferDec` slice from that frame and allocates each tile's `cur_sb_col` row-sync array for `max_sb_rows` integers. A worker then installs the current tile boundaries and begins parsing that attacker-controlled tile slice. Some internal row-mt decoder error occurs before the current-tile row is repaired in `xd->mi_row`; the staged patch shows four equivalent vulnerable exits with the same missing repair, but the saved artifacts do not reveal which one fired for this witness. `row_mt_worker_hook()` catches the longjmp and calls `signal_decoding_done_for_erroneous_row()`, which computes `sb_row_in_tile = ((xd->mi_row - tile->mi_row_start) >> mib_size_log2)` from the stale row and the current tile start. ASan reports the later write 44 bytes to the left of the raw malloc chunk backing `cur_sb_col`; because `aom_malloc()` returns an aligned interior pointer from that chunk, the saved artifacts prove this computed row index was negative and that `sync_write()` stored before the returned `cur_sb_col` array, producing the saved 4-byte heap-buffer-overflow write.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled tile payload and its bounds. `get_tile_buffer()` slices the current tile's byte range out of the decoded frame and stores that `(data,size)` pair in `TileBufferDec` for later row-mt parsing.
source.value_from: The staged 91-byte witness has SHA-256 `701077d30920e07d8053b4dc564a746db7669d5cb3c37a9d2f1357fc946a99bf`. In `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()`, byte 32 is `0x20`, so `threads == 33`; bytes 32..35 form little-endian `0x20202020`, so the harness truncates the frame to the remaining 47 bytes. The saved crash stack proves `av1_decode_tg_tiles_and_wrapup()` then dispatches that 47-byte frame into `decode_tiles_row_mt()`, whose `get_tile_buffer()` helper materializes the `TileBufferDec` slice consumed by the crashing worker.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `sync_write()` stores through the negative row index into the heap `cur_sb_col` array, producing the observed 4-byte heap-buffer-overflow write.
sink.note: ASan reports `WRITE of size 4` at this line, 44 bytes to the left of the raw malloc chunk allocated from `dec_row_mt_alloc:2496` to back the aligned `cur_sb_col` array.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The row-mt error signal derives the row index directly from `xd->mi_row` and the current tile start without validating that `xd->mi_row` still belongs to that tile. When an earlier internal error leaves `xd->mi_row` stale, this expression becomes negative and drives the out-of-bounds row-sync write.
root_cause.note: The staged patch resolves the invariant upstream by setting `xd->mi_row` before each vulnerable `aom_internal_error()` exit in `setup_bool_decoder()` and `decode_partition()`. The saved artifacts do not disambiguate which of those equivalent producers fired for this witness.

tainted_value_origin.description: This helper is the concrete origin of the tile payload and bounds later fed into the row-mt worker. Those bytes are what trigger the internal decoder error that leaves `xd->mi_row` stale before the negative-row signal path.

parser_admitted.description: The exact witness is admitted into the vulnerable row-mt tile decoder here. Step 0 makes `threads == 33`, `av1_dx_iface.c` defaults `row_mt = 1`, and Stage 01's crash stack includes `decode_tiles_row_mt()`.

evidence_limitations: The staged source checkout is commit `a92f3c847f445800e631a43bc2ab5894fedbc841`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `493cf67c62441838a56c5ea6f8dfbf6777e3cee7`; all line anchors therefore use the staged checkout's exact line map.

The saved artifacts prove the stale-`xd->mi_row` row-mt error-signaling bug and that the executed `sb_row_in_tile`/`r` was negative, but because `cur_sb_col` comes from aligned `aom_malloc()` storage they do not uniquely recover the exact integer slot from ASan's raw malloc-chunk bounds alone. They also do not reveal which of the four equivalent patched `aom_internal_error()` exits fired first. `run_flags.json` disables runtime disambiguation, so the fine trace grounds the shared missing obligation and the witnessed negative-index effect without inventing a single producer site or exact slot.

coarse_trace.summary: The exact 91-byte witness makes the harness request 33 decoder threads and pass one 47-byte frame into libaom, which then admits that frame into `decode_tiles_row_mt()` and materializes a `TileBufferDec` slice for a row-mt worker.

Row-mt computes `max_sb_rows`, allocates each tile's `cur_sb_col` array for that many integers, installs the current tile boundaries in `xd->tile`, and starts parsing the attacker-controlled tile slice.

An internal row-mt decoder error reaches the setjmp handler before `xd->mi_row` is valid for the current tile, so the erroneous-row signal derives a negative `sb_row_in_tile` from stale `xd->mi_row` and the current `tile->mi_row_start`.

`sync_write()` receives a negative `r`, takes the last-column signal path, and writes `cur_sb_col[r] = cur` before the returned heap row-sync array, matching ASan's write 44 bytes to the left of the raw malloc chunk that backs it.

fine_trace.note: Harness boundary. Byte 32 of the exact witness is `0x20`, so the decoder is configured with `threads == 33`, which is enough for the row-mt path later selected in project code.

Project admission to the vulnerable decoder path. `pbi->max_threads` inherits the harness value from step 0, `av1_dx_iface.c` defaults `row_mt = 1`, and the saved crash stack confirms that this branch dispatches the witness frame into `decode_tiles_row_mt()`.

Source. The frame bytes are split into a `TileBufferDec` slice for the current tile. The saved artifacts do not recover whether this witness took the explicit-size or last-tile branch, but either way this helper materializes the exact `(data,size)` pair later parsed by the crashing row-mt worker.

Row-mt computes the destination extent for per-tile row synchronization as `max_sb_rows`, the maximum superblock-row count over the current frame's tiles, and requests a fresh row-sync allocation when the cached size does not match.
Allocation context. `rows` is the `max_sb_rows` value from step 3, and `cur_sb_col` is the heap `int *` row-status array later indexed by `r` in the sink.

Before parsing the tile payload, the worker installs the current tile boundaries in `xd->tile`. `xd->tile.mi_row_start` is the current tile's top MI row and becomes the baseline subtracted from `xd->mi_row` on the erroneous-row signal path.

The current tile's attacker-controlled byte slice from step 2 is now bound to the row-mt bool decoder under the current tile boundaries from step 5. If any later row-mt validation fails while handling this tile, the setjmp handler in step 7 will run with whatever `xd->mi_row` is currently stored.

A row-mt internal decoder error longjmps here before `xd->mi_row` has been repaired for the current tile. The local fix commit and staged patch add that repair at four equivalent `aom_internal_error()` exits: the `read_is_valid` and `aom_reader_init` failures in `setup_bool_decoder()`, plus the two invalid-block checks in `decode_partition()`. The saved artifacts do not identify which of those exits fired for this witness; they do prove this handler then signaled the erroneous row with stale `xd->mi_row`.

Root-cause derivation. The erroneous-row helper subtracts the current tile's `mi_row_start` from stale `xd->mi_row` and treats the result as the row index inside this tile. The exact stale `xd->mi_row` value is not recovered from the saved artifacts, but step 11's write lands 44 bytes before the raw malloc chunk backing `cur_sb_col`; because `aom_malloc()` returns an aligned interior pointer from that chunk, this computation must have produced a negative `sb_row_in_tile` for the current tile.

The current tile's row-sync object is selected and the negative row index from step 8 is forwarded into `sync_write()` together with `c = sb_cols_in_tile - 1`, the last-column completion signal for the erroneous row.

Because step 9 passes `c = sb_cols_in_tile - 1`, the `else` arm executes, `cur` becomes `sb_cols + nsync`, and `sig` remains 1. That makes the write block execute unconditionally for the negative row index.

Sink. With negative `r`, this store lands before the returned `cur_sb_col` array. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting 4-byte heap-buffer-overflow write at this line 44 bytes to the left of the raw malloc region allocated at step 4; because `aom_malloc()` aligns the returned pointer inside that chunk, the saved artifacts prove the write occurred before `cur_sb_col[0]` but do not recover the exact element offset.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation stack identifies the same `cur_sb_col` backing storage later overwritten at the sink. The root cause is the negative `sb_row_in_tile` derivation at step 8 that drives a write before the returned `cur_sb_col` array.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Partially. The saved ASan stack exactly matches the fine-trace suffix `sync_write -> signal_decoding_done_for_erroneous_row -> row_mt_worker_hook -> decode_tiles_row_mt -> av1_decode_tg_tiles_and_wrapup -> read_one_tile_group_obu -> aom_decode_frame_from_obus -> av1_receive_compressed_data -> ...`. The earlier `aom_internal_error()` producer of stale `xd->mi_row` is hidden by the setjmp/longjmp control transfer, so that part is grounded by the staged patch and local fix-commit message rather than the sanitizer stack itself.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42508710 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` file to `/out/av1_dec_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` with `WRITE of size 4` at `sync_write`, stack `sync_write -> signal_decoding_done_for_erroneous_row -> row_mt_worker_hook`.

format.name: IVF-like AV1 decoder input
format.contract: Exactly the staged 91-byte file with SHA-256 `701077d30920e07d8053b4dc564a746db7669d5cb3c37a9d2f1357fc946a99bf`. For this exact witness, byte 32 is `0x20`, so `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` requests 33 decoder threads, and bytes 32..35 form little-endian `0x20202020`, which truncates to the remaining 47 bytes and yields one decoded frame. The saved artifacts prove that exact frame reaches `decode_tiles_row_mt()` and triggers the stale-`xd->mi_row` erroneous-row signal bug. They do not independently recover which tile-size branch `get_tile_buffer()` took or which of the four patched `aom_internal_error()` exits first produced the stale row, so this contract stays limited to the exact witness rather than a broader byte family.
